# Echo application reference input

Product-original R24-11 ARXML for one echo application component on the single-core ECU. The files preserve separate boundaries, including `unrelated.arxml`. The external R24-11 XSD and ECUC MOD archives stay under the ignored official-document directory and must not be copied here; external definition references resolve against the pinned local MOD archive. `manifest.json` records the raw bytes of every file, and `core/tests/official/reference_inputs.rs` validates the positive set and the negative copies against the XSD.

`types.arxml` describes the uint32 application/implementation mapping and the four-byte diagnostic OUT array. `application.arxml` has one application instance, explicit receive/send points, a 10 ms TimingEvent and the same component's synchronous server. `services.arxml` declares the Dcm service client. `extract.arxml` connects system signals, I-Signals, PDUs, frames, triggerings, communication ports and the target ECU. `ecuc.arxml` carries the selected OS/RTE/communication/diagnostic values. `bsw.arxml` identifies host implementation entries and their actual periodic entities; these entry names do not claim complete standardized BSW APIs.

R24-11 MOD module revisions are `4.10.0` (read from their DOC-REVISION), separately from the release name and `AUTOSAR_00053.xsd` schema identifier. `DcmDspDataByteSize=4` expresses the contract's 32-bit diagnostic element using the actual R24-11 parameter. Its OPAQUE representation prevents Dcm from exchanging the server's already big-endian bytes.

Diagnostic settings use 64-byte transport buffers, N_As/N_Bs/N_Cr = 200 ms, P2 = 50 ms, P2* = 5000 ms. Physical normal addressing, padding to DLC 8, and read-only DID 0x1234 are the fixed integration contract. S3 is a normative timeout, not an invented ECUC parameter.

Timing and negative-response conditions are explicit: `CanTpMainFunctionPeriod` and `DcmTaskTime` are 1 ms, `CanTpPaddingByte` is zero, `DcmDspMaxDidToRead` is two, and both global OS error-information switches are true. DSD subservices enable default/extended session control and TesterPresent subfunction zero (SWS_Dcm_00273). Repeating the configured DID twice produces a 13-byte UDS response for independent FF/CF/FC verification while using the same application operation.

The 17 BSW entries contain their actual return/argument descriptions. The `Host_*` base types bind existing C header declarations at the fixed x64 ABI; pointer declarations preserve pointer direction, and C array parameters use their adjusted pointer signature. These are host implementation types, separate from the application's uint32 mapping. Initialization entries use UNSPECIFIED execution context because StartupHook initialization is not Task context. Periodic entities require SCHEDULED/TASK as required by BSW Module Description Template `constr_4017`; the Com transmit entity is mapped after the application and before Dcm. A schema pass alone does not establish module obligations or generated C quality.
